A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete and readable, including equations, figures and tables. Despite renaming OTFusion to SOTA, they share the GMM-based optimal-transport fusion framework and original benchmarks. V1 has no appendix; v2 includes supplementary optimization, implementation and experimental material in Sections 6–8.

before.justification: V1 reports original OTFusion benchmark results, component ablations, parameter-sensitivity experiments and convergence analyses.

after.justification: V2 reports original SOTA results under transductive and inductive settings, with adaptive-weighting ablations, model-subset experiments and computational measurements. Some comparator results are explicitly attributed to earlier work.

M1.justification: V1 uses a linear OT objective with fixed model weights. V2 introduces squared agreement terms and MM-based adaptive weights, substantially changing optimization (Section 3.2.2 and Appendix 6). It also adds inductive inference using learned GMM parameters and fusion weights. Multi-model probability fusion and joint GMM/transport updates already existed in v1.

E1.justification: V2 retains the original 11 datasets, expands remote-sensing coverage from EuroSAT to ten datasets, and adds five medical-pathology datasets. It also evaluates inductive generalization to unseen instances alongside transduction. The claimed 26 benchmarks comprise overlapping domain groups: EuroSAT appears in both the natural-image and remote-sensing groups.

E2.justification: V2 substantially revises the evaluated comparator set. Table 1 adds GDA, ZLaP, Stat.A, ADAPT and GTA-CLIP; Table 4 adds Zero, MTA, TIPPLE, DPE and COSMIC. TransCLIP and ECALP remain, while TDA and DMN appear in the inductive comparison. V1's evaluated CoCoOp, TPT, DiffTPT, CuPL, Sus-X, VisDesc and CALIP comparisons disappear. Domain-specific individual models and simple ensemble comparators are also added.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a protocol that learns GMM parameters and weights on unlabeled training data and applies them to unseen test instances, whereas v1 evaluates transduction. It adds DINOv3 and additional model combinations, clustering-accuracy evaluations, and time/memory measurements. Appendix Table 6 specifies adaptation before ensembling. Exact inductive split sizes are not supplied, limiting reproduction of the new protocol.

E4.justification: V2 adds fixed-versus-adaptive weighting controls, a CLIP/MUSK disparity experiment, model-subset tests, clustering analyses and computational comparisons. Visual-source and joint-learning ablations extend questions already tested in v1. V1's feature-concatenation comparison, explicit single-visual-source ablations, epsilon/lambda sensitivity sweeps and convergence-loss plot disappear. The Pets visualization is replaced by EuroSAT/Food101 visualizations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, error bars or significance tests. V2's additional dataset averages and runtime measurements do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V1 Table 1 reports OTFusion averages of 74.95% and 70.45% for its two backbone settings. V2 Table 1 reports revised configurations, including 75.7% for CLIP-1+DINOv2 and 77.8% for CLIP-1+DINO(v2+v3), plus extensive new inductive and domain-specific results. These are not controlled same-setting improvements. Table 5 newly reports 71.8% fixed-weight versus 73.1% adaptive-weight accuracy.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's linear OT formulation and alternating updates, v2 derives a quadratic objective, a tangent minorizer in Theorem 1, adaptive coefficients and an MM optimization scheme. It adds a stationary-point convergence claim and computational-complexity analysis. The convergence argument does not establish that the stated GMM update increases the surrogate, so the added guarantee remains insufficiently justified.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes training-free transductive fusion and approximately ten-point improvements over CLIP. V2 broadens the contribution to adaptive, prior-free integration across model families, domains and inference settings, and explicitly claims applicability to black-box models accessed through APIs. Its novelty claim expands from VFM/VLM complementarity in transductive ZSL to foundation-model integration in zero-shot classification generally.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking adaptive weights to model agreement, interpreting modest gains among strong models and larger gains under model-quality disparities. It introduces modality-gap, model-subset and efficiency interpretations. V1's explicit limitation concerning fixed/equal weighting is replaced by claims of adaptive weighting, while future-work discussion shifts toward semantic ensemble learning and multi-view clustering.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the deferred code-release promise with a repository link and adds model-variant, weight-initialization and inductive-inference details in Appendix 7.2, directing readers to code for dataset templates. Most basic implementation information is retained: 224×224 center crops, fixed prompts, epsilon 0.01 and a 24GB RTX 4090. Repository availability is stated in the PDF but was not externally verified.

R1.justification: The related-work framing changes from inductive/transductive ZSL and Mixture of Experts to foundation models, VLM classification and optimal transport. V2 adds domain-specific foundation models, newer adaptation methods and MM-related literature, and explicitly acknowledges inspiration from TransCLIP. V1's discussion of DINO-assisted prompt learning and its MoE positioning are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution statements and substantial portions of the method and experimental narrative are rewritten. V2 introduces numbered subsections and a supplementary-material structure, moving optimization and implementation material there while expanding the main narrative around adaptive integration and inductive inference. This exceeds a method-name or terminology edit.

P2.justification: V2 adds a pipeline diagram, radial performance/clustering charts, grouped ablation bars and domain-specific comparison tables. The original backbone comparison and ablation tables are substantially reorganized, including separate transductive and inductive displays. Sensitivity and loss plots are removed, and the qualitative visualization becomes a two-dataset figure. Table styling and document layout also change extensively.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses v1's stated fixed-weight limitation and substantially strengthens the previously limited evidence for heterogeneous-model fusion through adaptive-weight controls, domain-specific ensembles, inductive evaluation and measured computational costs. These gains outweigh the loss of sensitivity analyses and reporting weaknesses. Nevertheless, the convergence justification is incomplete, Table 7 swaps the MUSK/PLIP baseline values relative to Table 3, and the claimed 6.9-point lead conflicts with Table 1: CLIP-1+DINOv3 exceeds GTA-CLIP by 2.9 points.
